clue.text: Space station with a name

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station in orbit from 1986 to 2001
'with' and 'and' both join one thing to another

explanation.surface: A space station named after someone, as if christening an orbiting outpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space station' looks like the definition, but it only supplies MIR; the definition is the last word, 'name'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Sweet timid sort welcomes sex

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mouse is a shy, timid person
S is an abbreviation for sex, as on forms

explanation.surface: A shy, sweet person who is open to sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the timid sort, but it is a noun: a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert, often chocolate, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Discovering it sends homeowner up the wall

definitions.text: Discovering it sends homeowner up the wall

parts.words: Discovering it sends homeowner up the wall
parts.note: the dampness literally climbs the wall, and finding it drives the owner up the wall, that is, infuriates them

explanation.surface: A homeowner is driven mad by finding something in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the wall' means furious, but it is also exactly where this moisture travels, drawn up through the brickwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundwater soaking upward through masonry is a common, costly defect in old houses.

clue.text: Colourful climber throws tantrums crossing icy Ural peaks

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cross over, enclosing the next two
the word tantrums is thrown about, scattering its letters into a new order
the peaks of the words are their tops, the first letters

explanation.surface: A mountaineer throws tantrums while crossing icy peaks of the Ural mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws' rearranges TANTRUMS and 'crossing' puts I and U, the tops of 'icy Ural', inside it. 'climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly flowered garden plant with trailing or climbing stems, orange and yellow blooms.

clue.text: Acting penfriend has no measure of dismay

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank

indicators.note: the penfriend lacks the measure, so those letters come out

parts.note: a pen pal is someone you write to
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A stand-in pen pal shows no sign of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes EN out of PENPAL, leaving PPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock or horrify someone is to fill them with dismay; both are verbs.

clue.text: Getting a partner rowing?

definitions.meaning: British slang: to be successfully attracting someone for a date or kiss
rowers pull on the oars; the question mark flags the playful sense

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether finding a partner is like taking a turn on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for picking someone up at a party, and literally the action of hauling oars through water.

clue.text: Casual piece — watch?

parts.note: a part is a piece of something
a timer measures time, as a watch does; the question mark admits the stretch

explanation.surface: A dress-down piece of jewellery or a watch, as if asking about a casual accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works only some hours is a casual worker rather than full-time.

clue.text: Provided the central element of this sentence

definitions.text: Provided the central element of this sentence

parts.words: Provided the central element of this sentence
parts.note: 'provided' means if, and those two letters sit at the centre of a word for a jail term served until death

explanation.surface: A grammar note: a word that supplied the key part of a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks like grammar, but it is a prison term; the clue points to IF, a synonym of 'Provided', at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term lasting the whole of the prisoner's remaining years is the most severe sentence.

clue.text: United's a member of football division

definitions.meaning: a club playing in a football league is one of its members

explanation.surface: A football club named United belongs to a division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a club name, as in Manchester United, but it means allied.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means conspiring together, and literally describes a club that belongs to a competition.

clue.text: First two of irritating Pogues' wayward followers

indicators.note: wayward means unruly and erratic, so the letters stray into a new order
the opening pair of letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Fans of the Irish folk-punk band the Pogues, some irritating and unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges IR, the first two letters of 'irritating', with POGUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted fans who trail after a band are a type of followers.

clue.text: Guardian nursing river country bear

indicators.note: something nursing holds another thing in its arms, so these letters go around the next piece

parts.note: the Guardian newspaper, home of this crossword, refers to itself as 'us'
the US is a country

explanation.surface: A newspaper caring for a bear from a rural or national setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' gives US because the clue is printed in that paper, which speaks of itself in the first person plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursus is the Latin genus name for the brown and black bears.

clue.text: Case of drink (oil of rum)

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of 'oil of' are made strange by rearranging

explanation.surface: A crate of drink, with a bracketed aside about oil of rum, like a shipping label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink in the case, but it is the anagram signal: OILOF rearranges to FOLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for loose papers or drawings.

clue.text: Pleasurable indulgence — sexed up element of Jane Austen work?

definitions.meaning: giving oneself over to the pleasures of the body and senses

definitions.text: sexed up element of Jane Austen work?
definitions.meaning: Austen wrote Sense and Sensibility; a racier version of that second word gives this one

explanation.surface: Indulgence described as a racy rewrite of a Jane Austen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful definition: swap the 'sensibility' of Austen's title for something steamier.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment of bodily, especially sexual, pleasure is what the word means; the Austen title supplies the joke.

clue.text: See 2
Walked like a confined prisoner in stockinged feet, which prevents self-harm

definitions.text: Walked like a confined prisoner in stockinged feet, which prevents self-harm

parts.words: Walked like a confined prisoner in stockinged feet, which prevents self-harm
parts.note: a prisoner walking in socks has padded about in a cell; the cushioned room itself keeps the inmate from injury

explanation.surface: A prisoner shuffles quietly about in socks, which keeps him from hurting himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as a past-tense verb and noun, padded plus cell; the whole describes a cushioned room for vulnerable inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: A room lined with soft material so an occupant cannot injure themselves against the walls.

clue.text: Linear DIY assistance that might be quickly withdrawn

definitions.text: Linear DIY assistance that might be quickly withdrawn

parts.words: Linear DIY assistance that might be quickly withdrawn
parts.note: a retractable steel rule for measuring lengths, which snaps back into its case

explanation.surface: Help with home improvement that could be rapidly taken back, like a cancelled offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' suggests an offer cancelled, but the spring-loaded strip literally whips back into its housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible measuring strip is a do-it-yourself tool for lengths, and it retracts quickly.

clue.text: Penguin's blueish ruffles breaking up pair?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters break up the pair, splitting it to sit between
to ruffle feathers is to disorder them, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A penguin's bluish feathers are ruffled while separating a mated pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffles' rearranges BLUEISH and 'breaking up' puts it between P and R. Penguin is the book firm, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin Books is a well-known company that issues books, so it is an example of the kind.

clue.text: Dish of pork topping and gold hog's back

indicators.note: the topping of a word is its first letter

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a hogback or hog's back is a long sharp ridge of hills, shaped like a pig's spine

explanation.surface: A meal of pork with a gold garnish, served on the back of the pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hog's Back is also a well-known ridge in Surrey, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal boiled in water or milk is a breakfast food served in a bowl.

clue.text: Fit a line to break the involuntary response

indicators.note: the line is put in to break up the word 'the'

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A tidy instruction about inserting a line, or a fit of involuntary reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like a seizure, matching 'involuntary response', but it means in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporty and physically in good condition, so healthy and strong.

clue.text: Published song by editor on the smaller side

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
a number is a song in a show or set

explanation.surface: A song that was released and edited, perhaps a short track.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fewer in number than the opposing side is the meaning, as in a vote or battle.

clue.text: Times cutting report base

indicators.note: the times cut into the report, going in its middle

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a boom
T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them stand for times

explanation.surface: Newspaper times reduce a report to its basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' and 'report' suggest a newspaper, but a report is a loud bang, and two Ts mean times.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest part of something is its foundation or underside.

clue.text: Remembered exactly Dicky having stroke

parts.note: British informal: dicky means unwell or unsound, as is off
to pat is to stroke gently

explanation.surface: Someone named Dicky suffering a stroke, recalled precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the British adjective for shaky or unwell, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something memorised perfectly is to know it word-perfect, the meaning of this idiom.

clue.text: Sides removed from metal framework channel

indicators.note: the two outer letters, the sides of the word, are taken away

parts.note: a grille is a grating or framework of metal bars

explanation.surface: Edges cut off a metal frame to leave a groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides removed from' strips the first and last letters, G and E, off GRILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stream or brook is a natural water channel.

clue.text: Aged female impersonator reverses tide to pat tomcat

indicators.note: the clue says these pieces are turned around, so the joined string is read backwards

parts.note: the flow is the incoming tide
to dab is to pat lightly
a gib is a tomcat, especially a castrated one

explanation.surface: An elderly drag artist turns back the sea in order to stroke a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' turns FLOWDABGIB, giving the three words of the answer. The definition refers to the wolf dressing as Little Red Riding Hood's grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the villain disguises himself as the grandmother, an old woman.

clue.text: Book scan reveals money

parts.note: to scan text is to read it

explanation.surface: Scanning a book uncovers some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang word for cash, from bread as the basic necessity one earns.

clue.text: Worthy attempt to use too much

parts.note: a go is an attempt
OD is short for overdose, to take too much

explanation.surface: A worthy effort to overindulge.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuous and deserving respect are both senses of being of moral merit.

clue.text: Hero cited fanciful four-syllable foot

indicators.note: fanciful means imaginatively invented, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A hero is quoted on some imaginative point of poetic metre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fanciful' rearranges HEROCITED. A trochee is stressed-unstressed; this foot is two of them together.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic metrical unit made of two trochees, so four syllables in all.

clue.text: "Drugs kill" bar

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet; ES is the plural
to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A warning slogan, drugs kill, posted in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a verb, to prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to stop someone asserting something is to bar or preclude them.

clue.text: One who concludes holding company is device to make text unreadable?

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it within

parts.note: someone who ends something is an ender

explanation.surface: Someone finishing a business deal, likened to a gadget that scrambles writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or program that converts plain messages into cipher makes them illegible to outsiders.

clue.text: Model imitation houses set boundaries

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: Imitation model houses, perhaps for a property development, with limits being drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is the verb signal that the answer sits inside 'Model imitation'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix the limits of something is to mark out where it ends.
